caseno: First Appeal No.424 of 2014 with Civil Rule No 1034(F) of 2014.
lawyer:
Sufia Ahmed, Advocate—For the Appellant. 
Md. Mesbahul Islam (Asif), Advocate—For the Respondent No. 1.
parties:
Alamgir Hossain (Md.) ----- Appellant
vs
Beauty Akter and anothers ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
Shahidul Karim J: This appeal is directed against the judgment and decree dated 28-08-2014 (decree signed on 3-9-2014) passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur in Family Suit No. 71 of 2010 decreeing the suit on contest. 

 2. Factual background leading to the filing of this appeal is that respondent Mossammat Beauty Akter as plaintiff instituted Family Suit No. 71 of 2010 against the defendant-appellant in the 5th Court of Assistant Judge-cum-Family court, Gazipur of realisation of dower money as well as maintenance. Upon receiving summons, the defendant-appellant entered appearance in the suit and contested the same by filing written statement denying all the material allegations made in the plaint while the suit reached at the stage of further hearing in the said Court, it was withdraw there form and transferred to the 2nd Court of Joint District Judge Gazipur for disposal by the learned District Judge, Gazipur vide his Memo No. 761 (2) 2 dated 16-10-2011. Thereafter, the learned Joint District judge concluded the trial of the suit upon taking evidence as well as hearing argument from both sides and ultimately decreed the suit on contest with a direction upon the defendant-appellant to pay off the dower money amounting to Taka 9 lacs including maintenance to the respondent-plaintiff by his judgment and order dated 28-8-2014. 

 3. Being aggrieved thereby and dissatisfied with the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-8-2014, the defendant-appellant preferred the instant appeal. 

 4. Mrs. Sufia Ahmed, learned Advocate appearing for the defendant-appellant has assailed the impugned judgment and decree critically contending that the learned joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur has or had no jurisdiction to try and dispose of a Family Suit which is exclusively friable by the Family Court constituted under the Family Court Ordinance, 1985 (in short, the Ordinance) and that being so, the impugned judgment and decree passed by the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur suffers from legal infirmity due to lack of jurisdiction. Referring to section 4 of the Ordinance, the learned Advocate further submits that all Courts of Assistant Judge in the country are now functioning as family Courts wherein the presiding judges are treated as Judges of the said Family Courts and there is nothing in the Ordinance which can show or at least suggest that the Courts of Joint District Judge will function as Family Courts. She also submits that since there is a specific provision in the Ordinance regarding transfer of a Family suit from one Family Court to another Family Court, the learned District Judge, Gazipur acted illegally in transferring the original Family Suit to the 2nd Court of Joint District Judge, Gazipur for disposal under section 24 of the Code of Civil Procedure (briefly, the Code) which provision has, in fact, no manner of application in Family Suit matters. Since the impugned judgment and decree has been passed by a Court who lacks in jurisdiction, the same is liable to be set-aside being the product of corum-non-judice, the learned Advocate finally yoked. 

 5. Mr. Md. Mesbahul Islam Asif, learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand, supports the impugned judgment and decree and contends that the same suffers from no illegality as the Joint District Judge did not arrogate the power of Family Court, rather he tried and disposed of the original Family Suit as it was transferred to him by the framed District Judge, Gazipur by invoking power under section 24 of the Code. The teamed Advocate further submits that the defendant-appellant did not raise any objection about the jurisdictional competency of the trial court while it was being tried therein, rather he conceded to the same and therefore, it does not lie in the mouth of the learned Advocate for the defendant-appellant to say now that the impugned judgment and decree is nothing but a nullity being passed by a court of incompetent jurisdiction. 

 6. We have considered the submissions advanced by the learned Advocates for both the parties, perused the memo of appeal along with the impugned judgment and decree dated 28-8-2014 including other connected materials available on record and also taken into consideration the facts and circumstances of the case as well as the law bearing on the subject extensively. 

 8. It further appears that initially the suit was filed before the 5th Court of Assistant Judge-cum-Family Court, Gazipur wherein the trial of the suit had already commended. At this stage, the suit was withdrawn from the above Family Court and it was transferred to the joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Gazipur for trial and disposal by the learned District Judge, Gazipur upon allowing an application filed by the defendant-appellant under section 24 of the Code and eventually the transferee Court decreed the suit. 

 10. From a bare reading of the aforesaid provision of law it is evident that a District Judge can transfer any family suit from one Family Court to another Family Court within the local limits of his jurisdiction. Thus, it can be said that in the presence of a definite and specific provision for transferring a family suit in the Ordinance, there is no scope to invoke the aid of section 24 of the Code whose applicability in family court's related matter has been forbidden by section 20 of the Ordinance as well. Furthermore, under the Ordinance the Courts of Joint District are not Family Courts and therefore, as a necessary corollary the Joint District Judges are not Judges of the Family Courts. Having regard to the aforesaid discussions, it is thus, evident that the impugned judgment and decree was passed by a court which had no jurisdiction to try and dispose of the matter in dispute between the parties. In other words, the impugned judgment and decree is bad in law being the product of corum-non-judice. 

 11. From our earlier discussion it is by now clear as day light that the legal infirmity or the stigma of lack of jurisdiction has been accrued to the impugned judgment and decree for no fault of the parties, but due to the utter ignorance as well as callousness of the concerned District Judge in dealing with the judicial function. The conduct of the District Judge in dealing with a family court related matter is not at all satisfactory, rather highly deplorable as because if the suit had not been transferred to the 2nd Court of Joint District Judge, Gazipur the controversy arose now could have easily been avoided. However, since the original family suit was filed for realization of dower and maintenance as far back as in the year 2010 and as the impugned judgment and decree suffers from lack of jurisdiction, which of course has occurred due to the fault of the District Judge concerned, ends of justice would be better served if the original family suit is sent back on remand to the 5th Court of Assistant Judge-Cum-Family Curt, Gazipur for trial and disposal upon setting aside the impugned judgment and decree. The learned Advocate for the plaintiff-respondent also candidly conceded to our above view. 

 13. Accordingly, the appeal is allowed on contest. The judgment and decree impugned against is set aside and the original Family Suit being No. 71 of 2010 is sent back on remand to the 5th Court of Assistant Judge-cum-Family Court, Gazipur for trial afresh in accordance with law. In the facts and circumstance of the case, the concerned judge of the Family Court is directed to dispose of the suit within 2 (two) months from the date of receipt of the record without giving any adjournment to either of the parties.
